title: Mexican Government Rules Out Cyclospora Contamination in Taylor Farms Lettuce in Mexico
author: Ángeles Cruz Martínez
content:
_This article by Ángeles Cruz Martínez originally appeared in the[July 23,
2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/23/politica/gobierno-
descarta-contaminacion-en-lechugas-de-taylor-farms-mexico-tras-inspeccion-
sanitaria), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.**

**The lettuce and water at the Taylor Farms de México, S. de R.L. de C.V.
plant are free of the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis, which causes explosive
diarrhea. Nor is there any presence of fecal coliforms, the Mexican government
reported.** The analysis was carried out by the National Reference Laboratory
of the Commission for Analytical Control and Coverage Expansion (CCAyAC) and
the State Public Health Laboratory of Guanajuato (LESP), and it determined
that the company operates within the physicochemical parameters established in
national standards.

It stated that from July 18 to 20, the Federal Commission for Protection
against Sanitary Risks (Cofepris) carried out an inspection and sanitary
verification visit to the plant, in coordination with epidemiologists and food
safety experts from the General Directorate of Epidemiology of the Ministry of
Health and from the National Service for Agri-Food Health, Safety, and Quality
(SENASICA) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development.

There, ten samples of iceberg lettuce were taken: 5 whole heads present at the
establishment and five samples of finished product: chopped, washed, and
disinfected lettuce; as well as four water samples for basic microbiological
and physicochemical determination. The company presented evidence of process
controls throughout the chain and of the application of food safety management
systems based on international recommendations. With respect to the irrigation
system, it was confirmed to be drip irrigation and that the plant's water
comes from its own certified wells.

The inspection also observed that Taylor Farms has a traceability system for
products and raw materials that allowed United States authorities to identify
the origin of the product and trace a batch held at the customs office in
Laredo, Texas, which never entered U.S. territory. From that batch the sample
was obtained that subsequently yielded a false positive result, according to
what the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reported last
Saturday.

For its part, Senasica made contact with lettuce producers that supply product
to the company and, although they hold a couple of certificates, they were
invited to obtain the Contamination Risk Reduction Systems (SRRC) certificate.
During the visit, personnel from the General Directorate of Epidemiology found
no health problems among the workers, nor outbreaks of diarrheal illness
requiring medical attention.
